title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_set<string> bankSet: up to N entries → O(N)
- unordered_set<string> visited: up to N+1 entries → O(N)
- queue<string> q: up to N+1 entries → O(N)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input strings, returned int
approach: Treat each gene string as a node in an implicit graph; two nodes are adjacent if they differ in exactly one of the 8 positions. Only strings in the bank (plus the start) are valid nodes. Run BFS from `startGene`; the first time we pop `endGene` the level counter is the minimum mutation count. BFS is correct because every edge has unit weight, so the first discovery of `endGene` is along a shortest path.
hints:
If you drew one node per gene string and connected two nodes whenever they differ in exactly one of the 8 positions, what classic graph question would "minimum mutations" become?
The bank has at most 10 entries, so even an exhaustive neighbor scan per node is cheap.

Breadth-first search on that implicit graph, using a hash set of the bank for O(1) validity checks. From "AACCGGTT", one neighbor in the bank is "AACCGGTA" (position 7: T→A), so it enters the queue at level 1.

**Start equals end** - startGene and endGene are identical and not in the bank
`Input: startGene = "AAAAAAAA", endGene = "AAAAAAAA", bank = []` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: `if (!bankSet.count(endGene)) return -1;` placed before the equality check → returns -1

**End not in bank** - endGene is absent from the bank
`Input: startGene = "AACCGGTT", endGene = "AACCGGTA", bank = ["AACCGGTC"]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: inserting endGene into bankSet unconditionally before BFS to "simplify" reachability → returns 1

**Disconnected bank** - bank genes exist but none chain from start to end
`Input: startGene = "AACCGGTT", endGene = "TTTTTTTT", bank = ["AACCGGTA","AACCGGTC"]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: returning `steps` instead of -1 when the queue empties → returns 2

**Direct single mutation** - endGene is one character from startGene and in the bank
`Input: startGene = "AACCGGTT", endGene = "AACCGGTA", bank = ["AACCGGTA"]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: re-evaluating `q.size()` inside the level loop `for (i=0; i<q.size(); i++)` and checking endGene at push time with `return steps` → returns 0

followUps.q: If bank.length can be up to 10^5, how does the approach change?
followUps.a: Keep the same BFS but switch to bidirectional search: expand the smaller frontier from start and end each round, stopping when a node appears in both visited sets. Time stays O(N·L·4) in the worst case but the explored set shrinks dramatically in practice; space remains O(N) for the two visited sets and the bank hash set.

followUps.q: If gene length L can be up to 10^5 (with N up to 10^5), generating all 4·L mutations per node is too slow - how do you build edges efficiently?
followUps.a: Use wildcard hashing: for each bank gene, replace each position with '*' to form L patterns, and group genes sharing a pattern in a hash map. Two genes sharing any pattern differ in exactly one position, so they are neighbors. Building the map is O(N·L) and BFS traversal is O(N·L) total; space is O(N·L) for the map.

followUps.q: If the bank is too large to hold in memory and arrives as a stream, how do you still answer the query?
followUps.a: Run bidirectional BFS but, instead of a preloaded hash set, filter the stream in passes: keep the current frontier, scan the stream once per level to emit only genes at Hamming distance 1 from some frontier node, and feed those into the next level. Time is O(passes · N · L) and space is O(frontier size), independent of total bank size.
